stories.headline: India’s e-mobility drive shifts mode as infrastructure takes charge
stories.deck: India’s e-mobility drive shifts mode as infrastructure takes charge
stories.bodyText: Bengaluru: The question around electric vehicles in India is no longer simply whether they will find buyers or make their way onto roads, but if the systems around them — batteries, charging, energy and economics — can keep pace with their growing presence..For a last-mile or gig-economy driver, it can come down to how much time a vehicle spends earning rather than charging. According to Battery Smart Co-founder and CEO Pulkit Khurana, “For high-utilisation two- and three-wheeler users, particularly those powering India’s last-mile and gig economy, uptime and economics are critical.”.His company’s Battery-as-a-Service model is built around that reality, reducing upfront battery costs and charging downtime, while allowing greater vehicle utilisation and earning potential. Battery Smart says it now has 325,000+ connected smart batteries across 90+ cities, serving 100,000+ drivers through 1,500+ battery stations, and enabling 4.5 billion+ clean kilometres..E3 Electric.AI brings AI-powered technology to electric scooters with TRION.For commercial vehicle operators, the calculation is broader, but no less practical. Government policies and incentives have played an important role in encouraging early electric-vehicle adoption, said Ganesh Mani, CEO of Switch Mobility. As the technology and ecosystem mature, however, “the focus is shifting towards total cost of ownership, lower operating costs and greater efficiency”..Mani expects private sector customers, including B2B logistics platforms and bus operators, to have a bigger role as electric bus penetration potentially reaches 10% by FY2028-29. For them, the question will be whether the numbers work..“At Tata Power, we are focused on expanding across highways, residential societies, workplaces and city hubs, while prioritising uptime and renewable integration,” said Virendra Goyal, Head – EV Charging, Tata Power. With 7,000+ public charging points, 2.5 lakh+ home chargers and 1,200+ e-bus charging points, the company aims to make EV charging seamless through digital tools that simplify locating, charging and paying..At the other end of the market, the nature of the customer conversation itself is changing. “The conversation is rapidly shifting from ‘Why electric?’ to ‘Which electric?’” said Hardeep Singh Brar, President and CEO of BMW Group India. One in four BMWs sold in India is now fully-electric, while the company’s EV portfolio grew nearly 80% in the first half of the year. With Neue Klasse (the carmaker's core technology and design platform for its next generation of EVs) coming to India, BMW says a range of over 800 km will be accompanied by a new generation of technology and driving experience..But none of these journeys can be separated from the energy that supports them. Omega Seiki Mobility Founder and Chairman Uday Narang mentioned that energy independence must remain at its core. "India’s clean-energy transition is no longer aspirational, with clean sources exceeding 331 GW of installed capacity. With Rs 2,000 crore under PM E-DRIVE, the focus must now be on taking reliable charging to Tier-II and III markets through PPPs, private investment and innovation,” he added..According to the Ministry of Heavy Industries, over 1.01 crore EVs sold in India to date, with 28.63 lakh vehicles supported under the PM E-DRIVE..Meanwhile, Eicher Trucks and Buses is building around that requirement, with close to 2,000 electric trucks and buses across diverse applications and more than 20,000 EV charging points integrated into its My Eicher app. Its wider sustainability efforts include green energy, rooftop solar and investments in H2ICE and hydrogen fuel cell technologies..As the industry marks World EV Day, the focus now is on ensuring that the infrastructure and economics keep pace with the growing presence of EVs on Indian roads.

stories.headline: Brazil vs India: Vinicius Jr, Raphinha set for historic Kolkata showdown
stories.deck: Brazil's new coach Carlo Ancelotti has named a 26-player squad for upcoming matches. The team will face Australia twice in September and then India. This selection marks a significant reshaping of the national team after their World Cup exit. Ancelotti is looking to integrate young talent for future tournaments. Brazil aims to rebuild its strength and challenge for the next World Cup.
stories.bodyText:
Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti has begun reshaping the national team after their disappointing 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign, naming a 26-man squad for the upcoming friendlies against Australia and India.
The squad includes some of Brazil's biggest names, with Real Madrid forward Vinícius Júnior, Barcelona winger Raphinha and Paris Saint-Germain veteran Marquinhos among the players selected by Ancelotti.
Brazil will begin their post-World Cup schedule with two meetings against Australia. The first is scheduled for September 25 at Queensland Country Bank Stadium in Townsville, followed by another clash with the hosts on September 29 at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane.
The five-time world champions will then travel to India for a historic fixture against the hosts on October 3. Brazil will face India for the first time in their history, with the match scheduled to begin at 7:30 PM IST at the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata.
Ancelotti begins Brazil overhaul
Ancelotti has made it clear that Brazil's next cycle will involve a significant reshaping of the squad, and his first selection since the World Cup reflects that approach.
The Italian coach has included several young players, with a number of them also eligible to represent Brazil at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. Ancelotti hopes the emerging group can eventually form the core of his side for the 2030 World Cup.
The coach had indicated in an interview with The Associated Press in July, shortly after Brazil's World Cup exit, that he intended to look towards younger players as part of the team's rebuilding process.
"Coach Carlo Ancelotti called up a total of 26 players on Wednesday (9) for Brazil's first matches after the World Cup. Ten of them play in Brazilian football. He released the list at the headquarters of the Brazilian Football Confederation, in Rio, from where he then gave a press conference," the CBF said in a statement.
The selection contains only a few of the players Ancelotti took to the World Cup three months ago, with the coach opting to introduce several fresh faces alongside established stars.
Brazil looking to move on from World Cup disappointment
Brazil's World Cup campaign ended in the round of 16 after they suffered defeat to Norway in their pre-quarters clash.
The result extended Brazil's wait for a sixth World Cup title. Their last triumph came in 2002, meaning the five-time champions have now gone without the trophy since their success in Japan and South Korea.
Ancelotti's first assignment after that disappointment will therefore be to begin rebuilding a squad capable of challenging at the next World Cup.
The upcoming Australia fixtures will provide his first opportunity to assess the new-look group before Brazil's historic meeting with India in Kolkata.

stories.headline: Teaching job aspirants protest in Prayagraj seeking recruitment
stories.deck: The Sanyukt Pratiyogi Chhatra Hunkar Manch, an organisation based in Prayagraj representing aspirants of competitive government recruitment examinations, has also expressed its support for the candidates.
stories.bodyText:
Teaching job aspirants in Prayagraj continued their indefinite sit-in protest on Wednesday (September 9, 2026) seeking notification for over 60,000 primary teachers’ posts. They accused the government of delaying vacancies for eight years.
“The vacancy of primary teachers is not advertised since the last eight years. This extended delay is negatively affecting our lives; we have commenced an indefinite sit-in protest at Pathar Girijaghar. We want the notification and time-bound recruitment of at least 60,000 teachers in government schools. This ongoing delay constitutes a criminal act as it kills the valuable years of young individuals,” said Rajat Singh, state president DELED Morcha. He further mentioned that candidates are maintaining communication through social media platforms. The Sanyukt Pratiyogi Chhatra Hunkar Manch, an organisation based in Prayagraj representing aspirants of competitive government recruitment examinations, has also expressed its support for the candidates.
Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) Rajya Sabha MP Sanjay Singh extended support to protesting teaching aspirants. “I visited the students’ protest site. Over 15 lakh unemployed D.El.Ed trained people are waiting for teacher recruitment for the last nine years while roughly two lakh posts of primary teachers are vacant in Uttar Pradesh. The state government has completely failed in conducting recruitment examinations. I urge the state government to please conduct recruitment. Sadly, in Uttar Pradesh the government is busy closing schools. I support these aspirants in every possible democratic way,” said Sanjay Singh, the Rajya Sabha MP.

stories.headline: Make govt sites user-friendly, PM Modi tells mantris
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi on Wednesday is learnt to have told ministers to make govt websites “user-friendly” to access information about welfare schemes and public services easily, and has advised Cabinet colleagues to be assertive while dealing with those who have made it their business of levelling unfair and baseless criticism.
PM’s direction to Cabinet ministers on improving govt portals comes barely months after cabinet secretary T V Somanthan advised all ministries and departments to overhaul their websites to make them easier to navigate. At the last council of ministers’ meeting, attended by all Union secretaries, Somanathan had referred to a report by The Economist that had flagged how govt websites in India remain difficult for ordinary citizens to use.
PM pushes for one-login govt portal
The report said that govt portals are cluttered with pop-ups, flashing banners and scrolling text, to name a few. It had also said that several websites work poorly on mobile phones despite most Indians using the internet through mobile phones.

briefs.headline: Seatbelt laws clear, enforcement is key: Supreme Court
briefs.deck: Seatbelt laws clear, enforcement is key: Supreme Court
briefs.bodyText: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Wednesday observed that adequate laws already mandated the wearing of seatbelts while a vehicle was in motion, and that ensuring compliance was the law-enforcement agencies' responsibility..A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the remarks while hearing a petition that sought directions for the mandatory use of seatbelts in vehicles..Counsel for the petitioner submitted that a large number of deaths and injuries in road accidents could be prevented if the existing seatbelt mandate was properly followed. He pointed out that many vehicles had non-functional seat belts due to fancy seat covers or other modifications..Fill the road safety gap in child health.“The law is very clear on seatbelts. The question is of implementation. How can we ensure that every citizen and every driver in this country complies with it?” the bench asked, adding that it was the law-enforcement agencies' duty to ensure compliance. .The court asked the petitioner to forward his suggestions to the competent authority..Referring to Rule 138(3) of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, the bench noted that the provision required the driver, the person seated in the front seat, and occupants of front-facing rear seats to wear seat belts while the vehicle was in motion..The petitioner’s counsel argued that public negligence and weak enforcement continued to result in serious injuries and fatalities across the country. .The court, however, observed that there were already sufficient laws on road-safety measures, including the mandatory use of seatbelts. .Non-compliance by citizens or enforcement agencies' failure to act against defaulters, it said, was essentially a matter of maintaining law and order..Disposing of the plea, the bench granted liberty to the petitioner to send a copy of his petition to the concerned authority for consideration of the suggestions contained in it.

briefs.headline: AI job cuts may rebound, forcing 30% rehired by 2029
briefs.deck: AI job cuts may rebound, forcing 30% rehired by 2029
briefs.bodyText: Bengaluru: Companies that are using AI primarily to cut headcount will end up paying a higher price to bring back the same talent. Gartner warns that by 2029, 30% of employees laid off due to AI replacement will need to be rehired, often at a significantly higher cost. With global labour force growth flat or declining, workforce cuts may deliver short-term financial gains, but they deplete talent pipelines and erode institutional knowledge, ultimately pushing up recruitment, training and onboarding costs..The technology insights company added a second warning that by 2027, 75% of organisations that prioritise capturing AI productivity gains purely as cost savings will be eclipsed by competitors that reinvest those gains into innovation, modernisation and upskilling. Gartner VP Analyst Tori Paulman said that when executives look back on the early AI era, they will realise their greatest mistake was believing work automation was the point, when workforce amplification was the opportunity..Gaming industry enters AI era with job cuts and new skills race.When that rehiring happens, it will not be an undo. The roles that were cut do not exist in the same form anymore.."Enterprises laid off roles, not tasks, and now they rehire for the context an employee is needed — human in the loop. Rehiring is for a supervisory role, not their old job," said Kabaleeswaran Sabapathi, Managing Enterprise Architect at Capgemini. He specialises in AI, digital transformation and governance..He said enterprises can do due diligence before cutting workforce only after identifying what AI can actually do and what still needs a human, and encourage reskilling before layoffs happen. That reality is echoed across staffing and advisory firms tracking the current wave.."When companies start rehiring after AI-driven layoffs, it won't just be a matter of hitting undo on past decisions. Those roles have changed forever," said Sridhar Krishnan, COO, MOAR Advisory.."People carry years of academic knowledge, deep workspace relationships, and that cannot be rebuilt overnight. If leaders view AI strictly as a tool to cut headcount, they run a massive risk of draining collective wisdom," he added..Recently, Oracle laid off over 20,000 people, citing AI deployment. Software company Atlassian also cut 10% of its workforce — around 1,600 — to self-fund further investment in AI..The pattern, according to ManpowerGroup India, resembles previous technology shifts: tasks are automated first, jobs are redesigned second, and new roles emerge around the technology. According to Shailesh Khanna, Brand Lead, ManpowerGroup India, many roles will not disappear completely. Instead, companies will need fewer people doing routine work and more people supervising AI systems, handling exceptions and making decisions. Recruiters become AI-assisted talent advisors, customer service agents become escalation and customer experience specialists, accountants become financial insight and AI-validation analysts, and HR coordinators become workforce analytics and employee experience specialists..At the same time, organisations are creating entirely new AI-era positions such as AI trainer, prompt engineer, AI governance specialist, AI auditor, human-AI workflow designer, data quality manager and AI adoption consultant. .AI layoffs could come back at a higher cost 30% Employees laid off due to AI may need to be rehired by 2029 75%Organisations focused only on AI cost savings risk being outpaced by 2027 20,000+Employees laid off by Oracle, citing AI deployment 1,600Jobs cut by Atlassian, or 10% of its workforce, to fund AI investment

briefs.headline: BJP claims ‘insult’ as Gujarat’s only Muslim MLA refuses to stand for newly-added lines of Vande Mataram
briefs.deck: BJP claims 'insult' as Gujarat’s only Muslim MLA sits out new Vande Mataram
briefs.bodyText: Ahmedabad: Imran Khedawala — the only Muslim in the 182-member Gujarat Assembly — on Wednesday refused to stand for the newly-added lines of the national song Vande Mataram, sung on the first day of the three-day monsoon session here in Gandhinagar..Defending his stand, the Congress MLA told DH: "I have great respect for the national song and for the portion that has been sung by our great leaders, from Mahatma Gandhi, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel, Rabindranath Tagore, and B R Ambedkar. If they never objected to that paragraph, who is the BJP to tell me anything?".He said he sat down in his seat after the additional paragraph of the song was sung. .Gandhi family considers itself above Constitution: BJP MP Anurag Thakur on Vande Mataram row.“The BJP is not bigger than Gandhi or Patel. Our leaders, including Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, and Rahul Gandhi, have made it clear. This is also my personal stand: I will not sing the additional paragraph,” Khedawala added..BJP leader and Minister of State for Forest, Environment, and Climate Change Pravin Mali, addressing reporters outside the Assembly, criticised Khedawala and the Congress for "disrespecting long-standing tradition".."There has been a tradition in the Assembly for years that its sessions start with Vande Mataram. Congress MLA Imran Khedawala stood but sat down immediately, which is an insult to the national song.".The saffron party accused Khedawala of disrespecting Vande Mataram, alleging that he "insulted the national song which was passed in Parliament as per the procedure laid down"..Khedawala represents the Jamalpur-Khadia constituency in Ahmedabad. He is the only Muslim MLA in Gujarat, which has a nearly 10% Muslim population..In 2012, there were only two Muslim MLAs in the Gujarat Assembly — both from the Congress. The number rose to three in 2017. Following the 2022 Assembly polls, Khedawala was the only Muslim representative in the house..Despite being in power for more than three decades, the BJP hasn't fielded a single candidate in the Assembly polls. .Since the demise of senior Congress leader Ahmed Patel in 2020, Gujarat has not seen a single leader from the community play a prominent role in national or local politics.

briefs.headline: West Asia conflict likely hindrance to cementing Brics declaration
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India’s push for agreement at the 
BRICS summit
 beginning Sept 12 faces divisions among its members over the West Asia conflict.
Russian officials, speaking to their country’s media, have acknowledged difficult negotiations, while Brazilian reporting has raised doubts about a strong final declaration. Yet Chinese commentary has highlighted opportunities for India’s presidency, including closer trade ties. These contrasting accounts suggest that the challenge for New Delhi is to keep economic cooperation moving while finding language that countries with conflicting security interests can accept.
The Sept 12–13 summit at Bharat Mandapam will bring these differences into focus. A final declaration records the common positions that participating countries have agreed to support.
Cannot predict outcome of declaration: Russian minister
Russian deputy foreign minister Sergey Ryabkov told TASS that some members were sharply critical of Tehran’s actions, making the Gulf situation Brics’ most pressing political issue. “And as of today, I cannot predict what the outcome will be,” he said about negotiations on the final document.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov acknowledged that Iran–UAE differences complicated drafting, but expressed confidence that diplomats would find acceptable wording.
The disagreement concerns what members want Brics to say about the conflict. Iran’s Mehr agency reported its judiciary chief’s call at a preparatory meeting for condemnation of US–Israeli attacks. UAE agency WAM highlighted Emirati criticism of Iranian attacks on commercial shipping and demands to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Share your thoughts in the comments
Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
Chinese commentary has focused on India’s economic strengths. A Global Times article carried by People’s Daily praised its strengths in digital techn and medicine, while saying that bridging differences among members would test Indian diplomacy.
Another Global Times commentary advocated deeper India–China trade and greater Chinese market access for Indian products. Indian reporting has highlighted New Delhi’s concerns about Chinese restrictions on critical technologies and industrial components.
In Brazil, CNN Brasil reported that President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva would prioritise poll campaigning and send foreign minister Mauro Vieira. South Africa’s Business Day questioned whether expansion had weakened Brics’ unity, while broadcaster SABC highlighted Pretoria’s push for trade, industrialisation and African infra investment.
For India, success would mean reaching useful agreements on specific issues while negotiating a common political message among partners whose interests do not always coincide.

briefs.headline: Safety norms can’t be retrospectively applied to older schools in Karnataka: House panel
briefs.deck: Safety norms can’t be retrospectively applied to older schools: House panel
briefs.bodyText: Government-aided and unaided schools established prior to 2017-18 must be exempted from stringent regulatory mechanisms and provided financial relaxation, the House Special Committee of the Karnataka Legislative Council headed by MLC Puttanna recommended to Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa..In the interim report submitted to the minister on Wednesday, the committee has also stressed the need to simplify the documentation process. One of the other major recommendations made by the committee is that current infrastructure and safety specifications cannot be retrospectively applied to older institutions..“Existing school buildings under 15 metres in height must be exempted from obtaining or renewing fire safety no-objection certificates (NOCs). The schools must, however, stock ABC/CO2 extinguishers, sand buckets, train staff for emergencies and ensure exit pathways are clear,” the committee said..Karnataka: Nearly 4,000 teachers in govt schools under old pension scheme.For school buildings taller than 15m, the committee has proposed extending the validity of the fire safety NOC from two years to five-ten years, besides recommending standardising the NOC fee, which the members felt must be brought down from Rs 20,000 to Rs 5,000. To eliminate corruption, the committee has recommended allowing government-registered civil engineers and architects to issue structural stability certificates to schools – these certificates will be valid for 25 years for buildings that are up to 25 years old, ten years for buildings aged between 25 and 35 years, and only five years for those that have been around for more than 35 years..The committee has also suggested halting the practice of demanding Rs 3,00,000 in security deposits or e-bank guarantees for renewing recognition. Instead, the committee recommended that the department honour the existing fixed deposit certificates for Rs 30,000. Taking issue with the inordinate amount of paperwork involved in the recognition process, which requires 30 documents, the committee suggested setting up two online portals on SATS – one for new schools to obtain approval and another for those established prior to 2017-18 to renew their recognition. Given that offering multi-curriculum education on the same campus is illegal, the committee recommended the ‘Safe Exit Rule’ for such schools, which the members felt would safeguard the interest of the students..To help students appearing for SSLC and PU examinations as private candidates, the committee recommended allowing provisional renewal for some schools.

briefs.headline: Can husband be tried for marital rape if law says not offence: Supreme Court
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Citing Article 20(1) of the Constitution which shields persons from prosecution for an act which is not an offence under existing penal laws, the 
Supreme Court
 on Wednesday asked whether a husband can be prosecuted for marital rape when the law categorically states that it is not an offence, even as it agreed with the Centre that the matter should be left for Parliament’s consideration.
Article 20(1) provides that “no person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of law in force at that time…” Section 375(2) of IPC said “sexual intercourse or sexual acts by a man with his wife, the wife not being under 15 years, is not rape” (wife’s age was raised to 18 by SC in 2017), with the provision replicated in Sect 63(2) of BNS.
Centre should go back to drawing board if law has a problem, says SC
With a bunch of petitions challenging the constitutional validity of this exception to rape, a bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the matter posed foundational questions, especially citing the case in which a husband has challenged a Karnataka high court decision to permit his prosecution for marital rape.
The hearing saw Solicitor General Tushar Mehta arguing that the issue, given its complexity, be left for the Parliament to consider.
It will be absurd for courts to take upon themselves the task of determining the nature of sex — natural or unnatural — when it is best left to people, their representatives and legislature, SG Tushar Mehta said.
Share your thoughts in the comments
Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
The bench agreed. “It should always come from Parliament. If the govt feels there is a problem with the law, then it should go back to the drawing board and recast the law with approval of Parliament,” it said.
During the last hearing, SC had wondered whether the court can rewrite penal laws to create a new offence.
Senior advocate Karuna Nundy said that no new offence needs to be created as the offence of rape is already defined and the only question is whether it is constitutionally justified to grant immunity from it to a class of persons (husbands).

stories.headline: Karnataka allows startups to pitch solutions to govt depts directly
stories.deck: Karnataka's government is adopting a 'govt-first' approach for startups. New policies aim to attract significant investments in aerospace and textiles. Startups can now pitch solutions directly to the government for consideration. The aerospace sector targets sixty thousand crore rupees in investments. Textile and garment industries will receive substantial government support and incentives.
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: A day before chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 completes 100 days in office, his administration adopted a “govt-first” approach, throwing open state departments to startups to pitch solutions directly to the govt to address Karnataka’s pressing social and administrative challenges.
At a cabinet meeting here Wednesday, the state govt approved a series of policies, including those for startups, aerospace, textile and readymade garments.
“Under the amended startup policy, the govt has decided to bring in a govt-first approach. Instead of waiting for technologies to be tested and proven by the private sector, we have decided to allow startups to come to the govt first to make a pitch,” said deputy chief minister G Parameshwara while briefing the media.
Sharing further details, IT-BT and home minister Priyank Kharge told TOI the decision was taken to allow startups a safe space to pitch their technology and products that are worth up to Rs 25 lakh.
However, riders will be in place to ensure that startups that come forward are credible. “The startups will have to come via govt-sponsored schemes such as Elevate or have credible funding track records,” Priyank added.
Job push, tech hub and much more
The cabinet also cleared the Aerospace policy 2026-2031, aiming to secure investments worth Rs 60,000 crore over five years.
The govt will grant incentives to companies that intend to invest in the state. Classifying the state into different zones, the govt has decided to provide subsidies of up to 30% for investments in focus areas, and up to 25% for non-focus areas.
“We are looking to secure Rs 60,000 crore in investments and provide employment to at least 50,000 people under the sector,” Parameshwara said.
The DCM cited the example of Tata systems planning to construct light combat aircraft (LCA) in association with Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL), which will see the govt provide certain incentives.
Under the new textile and readymade garments policy 2026-31, the govt will offer credit-linked incentives and power subsidy of up to Rs 2 per unit.
“We have identified 33 taluks for the textile and garment industry. The govt will spend up to Rs 4,000 crore in the next five years and earn investments worth Rs 20,000 crore,” Parameshwara further said.

stories.headline: As veterinary & farm science courses fill up, engineering seats pile up in Karnataka
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Veterinary and farm science courses have emerged as the most sought-after professional programmes in 
Karnataka
 this year, while engineering and nursing continue to struggle to fill seats, data from Karnataka Examinations Authority (KEA) shows.
Veterinary science has recorded zero vacancies for the second straight year. Agriculture and other farm science courses have seen a sharp turnaround in demand, with vacancies plunging from 7.1% (243 seats) in 2025 to under 0.5% (20 seats) this year, despite the total intake increasing by over 800.
Physiotherapy (BPT) too has witnessed a significant rise in demand, with the vacancy rate falling from 7.1% last year to 1.1% in 2026, leaving just 22 seats unfilled.
Pharmacy has seen improvement as well, though vacancies remain relatively high. The share of unfilled seats has declined from 20.8% in 2025 to 12.1% this year.
The picture is markedly different for engineering and architecture. Together, the two streams have recorded the largest increase in vacant seats — 9,453 more than last year. Their vacancy rate has risen from 18.1% to 26.3%, and a total of 24,856 seats remain unfilled this year. 
“The increase in vacancy is because of the increase in the number of seats available. Total seats increased from 85,020 to 94,318,” said H Prasanna, executive director of KEA.
Despite remaining among the most popular choices, computer science-related streams account for the largest share of vacant engineering seats. Computer science has 4,635 unfilled seats, followed by electronics and communication (3,570), mechanical engineering (2,635), civil engineering (2,488), information science and engineering (2,044), electrical and electronics (1,409), artificial intelligence and machine learning (1,014), and computer science and engineering (data science) (578).
One engineering college alone has more than 500 vacant seats, highlighting the uneven distribution of demand across institutions.
Nursing vacuum
The sharpest mismatch between available seats and student demand is seen in BSc Nursing, with the course recording a vacancy rate of 63% in 2026, leaving 22,831 seats unfilled — the highest among professional courses.
Yoga and naturopathy have also seen demand weaken, with vacancies rising from 37.5% to 41.1%.
Allied Health Sciences (AHS) presents a more nuanced picture, with intake jumping from 4,431 to 7,236 seats. Although the number of vacant seats is up by 122, the vacancy rate is down from 52.9% to 34.1%.
The data indicates that while some newer healthcare- and agriculture-linked courses are seeing stronger absorption, traditional high-volume courses such as engineering — particularly with a rapidly expanding seat pool — continue to struggle to match capacity with student demand.

stories.headline: Bengaluru’s Avenue Road houses one of its oldest antique stores, Balaji’s Antiques and Collectibles
stories.deck: Century-old Balaji’s Antiques and Collectibles in Bengaluru supplied props for A Passage to India, and houses artefacts from all over India
stories.bodyText:
When asked if he could recall a specific story about any of the artefacts they have collected or sold, DG Balaji, owner of Balaji’s Antiques and Collectibles, stares at the mini Dhara Pathra on his desk for a few seconds before finally admitting there are too many to choose from.
Balaji is the present owner of this century-old, family antique store in Bengaluru. His surroundings are a testament to his dilemma. As I entered the shop located in a labyrinth within the hustle and bustle of Avenue Road, it was clear every room here holds stories galore.
It started as the Seethaphone Company which sold gramophones and vinyl records in 1924, and was founded by DN Seetharama Shetty, DG Balaji’s grandfather. It was located just a few blocks away from the present day store in Avenue Road and is still functioning. Balaji’s Antiques and Collectibles branched out from Seethaphone Company in 1994. Today, Seethaphone is managed by Venkatesh Babu, and specialises in modern art and vinyl records. The reason for branching out, DG Balaji says, is because Seethaphone company was not interested in selling antiques.
The bounty at this rustic store takes me by surprise — artefacts, framed and unframed paintings, and other curios sit on shelves, while bootha masks, Marapachi and Dasara dolls, and lithographs of gods and goddesses gaze down from their perch on the walls.
David Lean visits Avenue Road
An interesting aspect of Balaji’s Antiques and Collectibles lies in a special client from the 1980s, during the production of David Lean’s acclaimed film A Passage to India (1984). When I asked about it, DG Balaji fondly remembers that he was eight or nine years old then. When I enquire if his parents told him of Lean’s visit, he says, “No, I met the team.” He recalls how Lean’s team initially wanted to rent the antiques as props, but once they realised Balaji’s were not keen on the idea, they purchased whatever they required. He has been assisting and witnessing the happenings at the Antique store from a very young age. Today, he is 58 years old and has the same unwavering passion for antiques.
“Colonial furniture was one of our most sought after items then,” he says, adding that could be one the reason the filmmakers reached out. “We supplied them with quite a few props; ranging from old newspapers to vintage cars, most of which can be seen in the film.”
Lessons from years of antiquing
Balaji finds the business of collectibles a meditative and evolving experience. “There is no one method behind finding antiques. Sometimes we go in search of them, at other times collectors come to us with requests. The process is not monotonous and is more mutual than it seems.”
He says there are no salaried teams or researchers on the lookout for antiques; they still rely on contacts garnered over the hundred years of its existence.
“However, there is more awareness today. People are interested in our history, traditions and culture, and as result, it has become harder to acquire antiques. The younger generation is not disposing heirlooms and keepsakes as they used to.”
Despite its impact on business, Balaji feels, “anything that has to do with our country and history must be preserved and protected.”

stories.headline: Bengaluru civic bodies collect half of annual property tax target, but weekly pace lags
stories.deck: The total weekly target is pegged at ₹103.99 crore
stories.bodyText:
For the fiscal year 2026–2027, the five corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) have a combined property tax revenue target of ₹6,700 crore, according to GBA data. By the end of August, the corporations had already collected ₹3,372.48 crore, which is 50.3% of the annual target.
Compared with the previous year’s collection for the same period, which stood at ₹3,211 crore, the corporations have achieved 5% higher revenue collection this year.
While there has been a minor increase, the new civic bodies are still struggling to maintain the required weekly pace, as they are able to achieve only 40% to 60% of the total weekly target, which is pegged at ₹103.99 crore.
According to the report, the city has 21,73,630 properties in the tax base, including residential, non-residential, mixed-use, and vacant properties. The actual revenue potential from these properties is pegged at ₹4,066.11 crore. The inclusion of arrears and revisions takes the target revenue to ₹6,700 crore.
Positive expansion, but not enough
The civic bodies have identified 3.19 lakh defaulters who owe the corporations ₹609.32 crore. In addition, the corporations have identified 32,215 cases under revision enforcement, which is expected to fetch ₹554 crore.
The figures indicate that the corporations are steadily expanding the property tax revenue base, even as they have failed to unlock new revenue avenues. Even last year, the final property tax collection was below ₹4,100 crore, leaving over ₹2,000 crore in arrears. However, the current trend indicates that tax collection is likely to cross the previous year’s figure.
Despite a good performance comparatively, enforcement needs to be tightened so that the corporations can significantly step up collections in the remaining months and stay on course to meet the annual target.
Positive about increase
A city corporation commissioner explained to The Hindu that the civic bodies are actively attempting to reach the target, as there is a high reliance on property tax to keep their revenue base healthy.
“During the civic budget, several works were planned, expecting revenue from avenues like the B-Khata conversion scheme and other sources. But many of those have not fetched the expected revenue, so we are trying our best to keep the available revenue streams healthy,” he explained.
The official further explained that despite a staff crunch due to several surveys, property tax collection has been better than last year. Once staff strength increases, the corporations are looking at tightening the collection and enforcement processes.
How the civic bodies fared
According to the data, the East Corporation has recorded the highest proportion of its target, collecting ₹882.22 crore, or 52.72%, of its target. West followed with ₹667.16 crore (52.06%), while South and Central have achieved 50.37% and 50.13%, respectively.
North has lagged behind the other corporations, collecting ₹565.56 crore, or 45.52%, of its ₹1,242.33-crore target. However, it has registered the highest year-on-year increase in collections at 9.15%.

briefs.headline: Two-wheeler ban on airport road, Electronics City flyovers temporarily put on hold by Bengaluru police
briefs.deck: Last week, the BTP announced restrictions on different categories of vehicles on five major elevated corridors in the city to improve road safety and traffic movement
briefs.bodyText:
The Bengaluru Traffic Police (BTP) on Tuesday announced that the ban on two-wheelers on the Airport Road and Electronics City elevated corridors has been temporarily put on hold after the pilot implementation led to congestion and traffic conflicts at diversion points.
The BTP has instead decided to implement vehicle restrictions on the two corridors in a phased manner. Last week, it announced restrictions on different categories of vehicles on five major elevated corridors in the city to improve road safety and traffic flow.
The restrictions on four flyovers, excluding the Electronics City Elevated Expressway, came into effect on September 4. A preliminary assessment found traffic movement on the BGS Flyover, Peenya Flyover and Double Decker Flyover to be smooth.
Longer queues and severe congestion
On the Airport Road Elevated Corridor between Sanjeevininagar Cross and Vidyashilpa Junction, the simultaneous diversion of goods vehicles, two-wheelers, and autorickshaws at the approach ramps led to long queues and severe congestion. The diversions also affected traffic flow on adjoining surface roads. While the restrictions were introduced to reduce accidents on these key flyovers, congestion on at-grade roads increased significantly.
As a result, the BTP said restrictions on goods vehicles on the Airport Road Elevated Corridor will continue during the notified hours in the first phase, while two-wheelers and autorickshaws will continue to be allowed on the corridor for now.
Two-wheeler advisory
The BTP has advised two-wheeler riders to predominantly use the leftmost lane, maintain lane discipline, avoid unsafe overtaking, and adhere to the prescribed speed limit of 60 kmph.
A similar phased approach will be adopted on the Electronics City Elevated Corridor from September 11. In the first phase, restrictions on goods vehicles will be enforced, while two-wheelers will continue to be permitted.
The two-wheeler restrictions will be introduced subsequently in a calibrated manner based on traffic flow, road-safety conditions, operational feasibility at approach ramps, and the impact on adjoining roads, the BTP said in a release.

stories.headline: RBI flags tech concentration risks, warns of disruptions
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: RBI deputy governor Rohit Jain flagged concentration risk among banks as most of them become dependent on a few cloud, technology and model providers, warning that a common technology dependency could allow a disruption at one provider to spread across multiple financial institutions.
Speaking at the Global Fintech Fest in Mumbai on Wednesday, Jain said emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, tokenisation, distributed technologies and quantum computing could make finance cheaper, more accessible and responsive, but could also amplify risks by increasing the speed, scale and interconnectedness of financial systems.
"I see three key concerns as emerging technologies become more deeply embedded in finance: speed, concentration and opacity," Jain said. "None of these risks is entirely new, but technology can amplify them and allow their effects to travel through the financial system in ways that are faster, wider and sometimes harder to detect."
On concentration, Jain said financial institutions could increasingly rely on a relatively small number of cloud providers, technology vendors and model providers, often using overlapping datasets and similar infrastructure. This, he said, meant that the failure of a common provider could become a financial-system problem rather than an isolated institutional failure. "The concern is therefore not simply the failure of one institution, but the possibility that a common dependency could transmit disruption or error across many institutions at the same time," he said.
"An institution may outsource the computation, but it cannot outsource the consequence," he said, adding: "Technology also does not eliminate traditional risks."

stories.headline: Coforge stock tumbles 6% as chairman Bhatt resigns
stories.deck: Co's Internal Audit Flags Concerns Over Board Evaluation
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Coforge shares dropped nearly 6% on BSE after chairman and independent director OP Bhatt resigned from the company's board with immediate effect on Tuesday. The resignation followed an internal audit review that raised concerns about how the company's board evaluation exercise was handled and presented. Bhatt became chairman of Coforge in 2024. He previously served as chairman of State Bank of India from 2006 to 2011.
Coforge said the internal audit, conducted as part of its plan for the Sept quarter of FY26, identified concerns relating to the Board Evaluation Report (BER). These included the non-disclosure of certain material information relating to the report and the chairman's performance when it was presented to the board.
The board subsequently raised its concerns with Bhatt and sought an explanation. While Bhatt responded, the board was still evaluating his explanation and had not taken any final decision when he resigned on Sept 8.
"The Board considers it important to clarify that the chairman's resignation followed the concerns identified in the internal audit review and the subsequent process undertaken by the Board to seek and consider his explanation," Coforge said in its regulatory filing.
In his resignation email, Bhatt said he had considered the matters raised concerning the board evaluation process and the circumstances that followed.
"I believe that continuing on the Board while there remains a disagreement considering the characteristics of my good faith actions in the Board evaluation process would not be conducive to the effective functioning of the Board," Bhatt said.
He added that the matters relating to the board evaluation process were the material reasons for his resignation and that there were no other material reasons. Bhatt said he had served as an independent director and chairman with a "strong sense of responsibility" and had sought to discharge his duties independently and objectively, while balancing the interests of shareholders, management and the company.
Coforge has designated non-executive independent director Vivek Sharma as interim chairperson until Jan 31, 2027. Bhatt will also cease to be a member of the company's board committees with immediate effect.
The resignation follows a shareholder vote last month in which investors rejected Bhatt's reappointment as an independent director. At the company's 34th annual general meeting on Aug 24, the special resolution received 65.4% votes in favour and 34.5% against, failing to secure the required majority. "It looks like disagreements on strategy and policy matters between the chairman and the largest shareholder, Advent, seem to have led to this resignation.
"The reappointment of OP Bhatt effective May 2027 put to vote at the Aug 24 AGM was voted against, with Advent, the largest shareholder voting against," said Shriram Subramanian, MD of corporate governance research firm InGovern Research Services.

stories.headline: Indian photonics industry forms association amid AI boom
stories.deck: The newly formed Indian Photonics Association (IPA) estimated that its products, key in AI data centres and telecom networks, would be worth billions of dollars in the country by 2031
stories.bodyText:
A handful of firms in the photonics industry have formed the Indian Photonics Association (IPA), a grouping of firms that work on the technology. The move comes as the Union government also seeks to promote, through the India Semiconductor Mission’s second phase, the domestic manufacture of photonics products like transceivers, which sit at the end of fiber-optic cables, forming a crucial component in telecom networks and AI data centres.
Photonics has boomed particularly since AI data centres need a large number of high-speed interconnections both internally and with the outside world. “The photonics industry knew it; the others took some time to catch up,” Tarun Sibal, the founder of Noida-based CloudPhotonix, said in an interview with The Hindu in July. “The industry realised that if you are creating an AI stack, the AI stack is not just servers and data centres… How do you get the throughput for that level of compute? And I think that set the cat amongst the pigeons.”
Ashwini Aggarwal, the IPA’s inaugural director general, said that firms from across the country had joined the IPA. “India has BharatNet, which is one of the world’s largest optical fibre networks; we have ISRO, it is actually delivering optical payloads between the satellites; we have a data centre industry coming up which is just [booming],” he said in an interview on the sidelines of the launch. “We have optical transceivers and photonics-based interfaces coming up rapidly in that ecosystem. Imagine all this is happening and we don’t have a community body to actually give a voice to what is required for the industry.”
Rohin Y., an IPA board member and founder of LightSpeed Photonics, said that the need to develop the indigenous industry was urgent. “Many months ago there was one LinkedIn [post] that went viral by a photonics founder, which was taken down very soon later, with a very lengthy message which was kind of very saddening to hear — that he wanted to for six months start something in photonics in the nation and he tried and what not… He said ‘I quit. I am going to China.’ I was very much left in a bad taste,” he said at the launch.
“It was very unfortunate that they didn’t have an ecosystem to fall back [on],” he told The Hindu. “And that is what we wanted to have, where there is an end-to-end ecosystem and local supply chain, just like China has that kind of a model, where you have anchor customers who are enabling the rest of the ecosystem.”
Domestic photonics players face stiff competition from China, Mr. Sibal pointed out. “I am subject to the same price as China, because my competitor is an importer who has no physical infrastructure,” he said in July.
While IPA’s founders pitched government engagement as just one aspect, the industry may have a lot to engage the IT Ministry and other government bodies on. Mr. Sibal pointed in July to the friction-ridden process of getting his manufacturing operations going. “You go to a Vietnam or a China, they are plug and play,” he said.
“You just walk in with your brains and a little bit of your equipment and you are running. You’re not worried about how I’ll get electricity, or whether I’m talking to the transformer guy to stabilise the voltage, or writing to the electricity department to ask, will you give me the adequate supply, will I have the sanctioned load I need? Which is a distraction, because by the time you sort these problems out, you’re pushing out your actual production.”
Mr. Sibal pointed out that even though his firm had filled its order books for months — “demand is not a problem,” he insisted — bankers unfamiliar with the industry were reluctant to provide operational expenditure financing, a problem that may be affecting many players in the less noticeable parts of the electronics manufacturing industry.
The IPA said in a two-page note that it estimated the Indian photonics industry to be worth anywhere between $6.8 billion to $7.93 billion by 2031. The “value chain remains thin” on “advanced detectors, laser sources and optical engines,” the note said. Many of the components and materials used by Indian players remain imported, even as some try to indigenise production more deeply.

stories.headline: PM-KUSUM 2.0 announcement likely soon; agrivoltaics to get dedicated component
stories.deck: Launched in 2019, PM-KUSUM seeks to expand the use of solar energy in agriculture.

The second phase of the Centre’s flagship PM-KUSUM scheme is likely to be announced shortly, Union Minister for New and Renewable Energy Pralhad Joshi said on the sidelines of the curtain raiser for the seventh Agrivoltaics World Conference 2026.
“The process is on for PM-KUSUM 2.0, that is, Phase-II, and I am quite confident very shortly the honourable Prime Minister [will make the announcement],” Joshi told reporters.
Addressing the conference, the minister said the next phase of the scheme would include a dedicated component for agrivoltaics, which combines agricultural activity with solar power generation.
Joshi said the government’s broader focus would remain on supporting small and marginal farmers, farmer producer organisations (FPOs), cooperatives and panchayats as the country expands the use of renewable energy in agriculture.
He also called on industry stakeholders and researchers to deepen studies on agrivoltaic applications, particularly their suitability across different crops, climatic conditions and geographical regions.
“We need much more research. We need to understand what works best for different crops, climate and regions. One formula cannot work everywhere,” Joshi said, stressing the need for a “deeper study”.
Launched in 2019, the Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan (PM-KUSUM) aims to increase the use of solar energy in agriculture. The scheme supports the installation of decentralised solar power plants, standalone solar-powered agricultural pumps and the solarisation of grid-connected agricultural pumps.

briefs.headline: Sensex tanks 813 points as crude spikes
briefs.deck: Rupee Feels Heat Too, Slips To Over 95/$; Foreign Funds Sell
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Rising geopolitical tensions in the Persian Gulf region pushed up Brent prices above the $100-per-barrel mark for the first time since July on Wednesday. This, in turn, led to the weakening of the rupee, which fell below the 95/$ mark and settled at 95.1 at close. Dalal Street, too, felt the jitters courtesy of these developments, with investors pressing the sell button, resulting in 
sensex
 falling below the 75K mark after nearly three months.
With foreign funds selling aggressively, the benchmark index closed 813 points lower at 74,764 points. 
HDFC Bank
 and 
Infosys
 contributed the most to the day's losses. On NSE, Nifty lost 204 points (0.9%) to close at 23,432 points.
In the last one month, sensex has lost nearly 3,800 points or 4.8%, while Nifty is down 1,152 points or 4.7%. The losses came on the back of muted foreign fund activity through this one-month period. Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), however, have again turned aggressive sellers in Sept. After two months of net inflows, FPIs have net sold stocks worth around Rs 12,400 crore in India, so far this month, combined data from NSDL and BSE showed.
A revival in Chinese demand for crude also helped the rally in oil prices, reports said. 
Bond yields in US, where the yield on the 10-year Treasury (govt) bonds crossed the 4.8%-per-annum mark again, led market players to believe there's a high chance it may soon move closer to the 5% mark, adding to the worry of investors.
Against this backdrop-rising oil prices which could stoke inflation and rising bond yields-US Federal Reserve's policy-setting meeting next week, with its rate decision set for Sept 16, is turning out to be an extremely important one for the market. Any indication of a rate hike in US could have global implications, market players here said.
According to Vinod Nair of Geojit Investments, markets are increasingly pricing in a prolonged West Asia conflict, with continued hostilities and retaliatory actions expected to keep crude oil prices elevated in the near term. "Persistent geopolitical uncertainty is making it difficult for major central banks to achieve a balance between growth and inflation," he said.
On the sectoral front, software services stocks led the slide. "The Nifty IT index declined around 3%, as rising US bond yields, concerns over US Federal Reserve's rate outlook and structural worries around AI-driven disruption weighed on technology stocks," said Ajit Mishra of Religare Broking. "Realty, financials and FMCG also edged lower, while select defence, metal and energy-related stocks showed relative resilience."

briefs.headline: Cognizant's green card filings suspended amid probe by US
briefs.bodyText:
BENGALURU: Cognizant's US green-card filings have been suspended amid an investigation into potential fraud and misuse of employment visa programmes, Anthony D'Esposito, inspector general at US Department of Labor, said in a post on X. "Fighting fraud is a Team Sport.....Threats to American workers will not be tolerated. Alongside @WHFraudTF, we're following facts, fraud and finances. Handcuffs await," he posted on X.
The move could further complicate the immigration outlook for Cognizant's foreign employees, many of whom already face prolonged waits and uncertainty over obtaining permanent residency and, eventually, citizenship in US. It could also raise questions among clients about how the company will staff projects requiring specialised skills if the suspension affects the movement or long-term status of foreign workers.
Companies generally do not disclose how many employees have received US green cards or how many are currently in the green-card sponsorship process, making it difficult to assess the number of workers directly affected by the suspension.
The suspension comes a day after Cognizant announced plans to hire 1,500 US college graduates and expand its frontier certified engineer and frontier business operator workforce to 15,000 people.
In July, US Department of Labor launched a nationwide investigation into alleged fraud involving the H-1B and PERM employment visa programmes.

briefs.headline: NSE cuts IPO size, may raise 23.5k crore
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: IPO-bound National Stock Exchange (NSE), the largest stock exchange in India by turnover and profits, is reducing the size of its offering to about 5.3% of its equity base, from 6% planned earlier. The stocks will be offered in a price band of Rs 1,700 to Rs 1,785 per share, people in the know said.
In effect, the reduced size and also the price band would together cut the offer size to about Rs 23,500 crore. Earlier, NSE's IPO was expected to raise about Rs 30,000 crore, which would have made it the largest current public listing in India.
According to people in the know, even during pre-IPO days when NSE management was persuading its shareholders to offer their shares in the IPO, very few were willing to sell their stakes in the offer. They were willing to hold on to the shares, see the post-IPO price on the bourse and once the lock-in was to end, decide about their holdings, a source said.
At the upper end of the reduced price band, NSE would be valued at about Rs 4.4 lakh crore, down from an earlier estimate of about Rs 5 lakh crore.
On Sept 4, markets regulator Sebi cleared NSE's IPO documents. Earlier, existing shareholders together were selling nearly 15 crore shares, which is now being reduced to about 13.2 crore shares. 
Market participants said the offer would be launched "as soon as possible". And according to merchant banking sources, the offer could open as soon as Sept 16.
Currently, in the unofficial space for trading of shares, NSE is quoting between Rs 1,950 and Rs 2,050. In the same market, the grey market premium (GMP)-the estimated premium that the share could command at listing-has been fluctuating over the last few days.

briefs.headline: Skoda Auto, JSW sign MoU to explore PV joint venture

NEW DELHI: 
Skoda Auto
 and JSW Green Mobility have signed a non-binding agreement to explore a joint venture that could develop, manufacture and sell passenger vehicles in India and overseas, the companies announced on Wednesday. The proposed partnership will span internal combustion engine vehicles, 
electric vehicles
, plug-in hybrids and hybrids, signalling that the discussions extend beyond an electric mobility alliance.
"At this stage, the MoU is exploratory and non-binding. The two companies are in early discussions, and there is no definitive agreement yet," a JSW Group spokesperson said. Any binding arrangement will require further negotiations, internal approvals and regulatory clearances, the spokesperson added. The companies did not disclose the proposed investment, shareholding structure or timelines for concluding the negotiations.
Skoda Auto, which leads Volkswagen Group's operations in India, said the proposed two-party partnership would have joint control, with clearly defined responsibilities and mechanisms for faster decision-making.
The collaboration is expected to focus on widening the product portfolio, increasing localisation and strengthening manufacturing and research and development capabilities in India. Platform synergies and deeper localisation are also expected to help the companies offer more competitively priced vehicles, build scale and improve profitability. "To fully explore the country's growth potential, we are always considering new business opportunities," the spokesperson said.

briefs.headline: With iPhone Duo, Apple makes entry into foldable market
briefs.deck: Takes On Samsung, Google | Launches iPhone 18 Pro Series
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Apple on Wednesday entered the foldable smartphone market with iPhone Duo, priced at Rs 2,99,900, taking on Samsung, Google and Chinese brands in a category it had stayed away from even as rivals spent years refining the form factor.
The book-style device has a 5.5-inch outer screen and unfolds into a 7.8-inch display, effectively turning the phone into a small tablet. It supports side-by-side apps, enhanced multi-tasking and the Apple Pencil, while Touch ID returns through the power button, instead of Face ID. iPhone Duo pre-orders open in India on Oct 16, with retail availability beginning on Oct 23.
Apple also launched the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max at Rs 1,64,900 and Rs 1,79,900, respectively. Pre-orders in India begin Sept 12, with sales starting Sept 18. Both models are available with up to 2TB storage.
Their headline upgrade is a 48MP main camera with variable aperture, allowing users to control depth of field and light intake. Apple has added manual controls for aperture, shutter speed and white balance, along with reference image, a feature that records signed sensor data to help establish whether a photograph has been altered.
The phones use the 2-nanometre A20 Pro chip and a larger vapour chamber for thermal management. Apple claims up to 40% faster graphics performance, though real-world gains will require independent testing. The company promises up to 36 hours of video playback on the Pro and 45 hours on the Pro Max for eSIM-only variants.
Siri AI, arriving in beta with iOS 27, can use information from messages, emails and photographs to answer questions and perform tasks. However, availability will initially vary by language and region, while some cloud-based AI functions will carry daily usage limits.
Apple also unveiled Watch Ultra 4 at Rs 1,09,900. It adds a readiness score, more frequent heart-rate and HRV measurements, and battery life of up to 50 hours. Its audio intelligence features will arrive in beta later this year.

briefs.headline: Adani Airports to raise $1 billion equity from global investors
briefs.deck: Co Valued At $18Bn, One Of Largest Bets From FIs In Sector
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: India's largest private airport operator - Adani Airport Holdings (AAHL) - has entered into binding agreements to raise Rs 9,825 crore (about $1 billion) of primary equity capital from a consortium of investors, comprising Alpha Wave Global, Premji Invest, Temasek and BlackRock managed funds. The transaction values AAHL at about $18 billion and is one of the largest primary equity investments from financial institutions in India's airport infrastructure sector.
AAHL and the investors have entered into a share subscription agreement and a shareholders' agreement pursuant to which the investors will subscribe to new equity shares of AAHL in three tranches, with the final tranche expected to be completed by July 2027. Investors will collectively hold over 5.5% in AAHL. The latest transaction follows AEL's successful Rs 15,000 crore QIP in July 2026.
The company said these proceeds will support three strategic priorities - expanding and modernising airport infrastructure across AAHL's portfolio; accelerating the development of integrated Adani airport city ecosystems around its airports with development of about 2.2 crore square feet of mixed-use development planned in the first phase; and scaling up of passenger-facing and other non-aeronautical businesses, including its ground handling business.
AAHL manages eight airports across India - Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Jaipur, Lucknow, Guwahati, Mangaluru and Thiruvananthapuram - handling over 23% of India's total passenger traffic. "These investments are expected to increase capacity to serve 20 crore passengers annually, deepen commercial monetisation, enhance passenger experience and further strengthen AAHL's integrated airport ecosystem," AAHL, a subsidiary of Adani Enterprises (AEL), said in a statement.
AAHL non-executive director Jeet Adani said: "With the backing of these partners, we will continue to invest ahead of that growth, scaling our infrastructure, city-side developments and non-aeronautical businesses to build one of the world's leading integrated airport platforms."

stories.headline: 'A ball won't kill you, but bullets can': Rashid Khan on childhood in Afghanistan
stories.deck: As Afghanistan prepare to face India in a three-match T20I series, starting Sunday at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi, star all-rounder Rashid Khan opened up about the challenges he faced as a child in the war-torn country and how those experiences helped shape his mindset.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: From a war-torn nation to making a mark on the world stage, Afghanistan cricket has come a long way. The team has produced stunning performances, challenged some of the best sides in the world and pulled off big wins against top teams. Once seen as minnows, Afghanistan have slowly shed that tag and emerged as a team capable of becoming a nightmare for the opposition.
As Afghanistan prepare to face India in a three-match T20I series, starting Sunday at the Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi, star all-rounder 
Rashid Khan
 opened up about the challenges he faced as a child in the war-torn country and how those experiences helped shape his mindset.
Rashid is part of the Afghanistan T20I squad for the series against India, with all three matches scheduled to be played in Delhi.
During a podcast, The Parenting Pause, Rashid was asked: "You were born into a country which had some level of conflict. There was sort of war. There was some instability. Your memories?"
“Well, I think this cricket is just a normal thing, you know. And as I mentioned, what our parents have gone through, when they share their life experience with us, we are, like, you know, so blessed. This is nothing. This pressure is nothing. 
What we are doing in our life is nothing compared to what they have gone through. You know how it was in Afghanistan 30 years back, 35 years back, and in those days how our parents struggled in the war, like, you know, 40 years back," Rashid said.
“My mom and dad, they share their experience — how we went from this place to that place and how hard it was for them to go through all those things. So I was like, they have seen bullets going up in the air. For us to see a ball going up in the air, that is just easy. You know, it won't kill you, but that can kill you. So, to have that kind of mentality — it's just nothing, you just need to go for it — you can do it. You won't die. It's not something that you're going to die from. And you just need to have a strong mindset.
Rashid said the mental strength he has developed over the years came largely from watching his parents deal with difficult situations.
“And I feel it's all come from my parents. You know, what kind of mindset they had, how strong they were at that particular time, you know, to help and to raise your kids as well in having those kind of tough situations. I think they were the strongest, and I feel like we just got that mentality from our parents.
“And whenever facing any tough days, tough time, I just think about how tough that would have been. But they never let themselves down. So why should I let myself down with this pressure?
Rashid said remembering what his parents went through helps him put pressure and difficult moments into perspective.
“So I think it just all comes mentally, like, you know, to have those things in the mind, and then you become mentally stronger. So yeah, I think I feel I keep that with myself, and it just helps me in a tougher time. It just helps me, and everything just goes in seconds when I think about it. You put everything in perspective. Yeah. So nothing remains.
“It's just like, okay, there is a saying now, and they say that what doesn't kill you only makes you stronger.”
Rashid believes difficult situations can also become opportunities to learn and grow.
"It only teaches you and makes you stronger and gives you a better listener. So I think in a pressure situation, tough situation, you know, I'm so happy for that time because it's not only the pressure situation, it's just the best time for me to learn and to get the good experience and to become a better person, physically and mentally," he said.

stories.headline: Pipers put it across Masters, remain in joint lead
stories.bodyText:
The Bangalore Golf Club is just across the road. That suits Magnus Carlsen fine. He could come to Lalit Ashok, the venue of the Tech Mahindra Global Chess League, after his golfing stint at the course.
He spent quite a few hours there on Wednesday, longer than usual, apparently. The fresh air and the green fields seemed to have helped, as he came up with a fine win against Maxime Vachier-Lagrave.
It was the World No. 1’s second win in the tournament, though he may not have enjoyed his first as much; in the game against Viswanathan Anand, he emerged victorious only because his old World championship rival ran out of time when the position was equal.
Carlsen needed no such help from the clock against Vachier-Lagrave.
His team, Alpine APL Pipers, won the match against Cheq Mumba Masters 11-6. The highlight of the match was Anish Giri’s spectacular victory against M. Pranesh.
The win helped the Pipers retain their joint lead. They have 12 match points, the same as Fyers American Gambits and Ganges Grandmasters.
Gambits are more equal at the moment than the others, as they have 60 game points, two more than Pipers. Grandmasters are on 55.
Mumba Masters and PBG Alaskan Knights have nine match points each. But it was another dismal day for the two-time champion Triveni Continental Kings, which lost both matches and is lying at the bottom of the table with nine match points.

stories.headline: Pratika’s India comeback gets boost as she replaces injured Jemimah for Asian Games
stories.deck: With Jemimah Rodrigues sidelined due to a hamstring injury from The Hundred, Pratika Rawal has been selected to join India's squad for the upcoming Asian Games. Rawal made her T20I debut in the ongoing Asia Cup, adding fresh talent to the team. India will defend its title in the women's cricket event from September 17 to 22 in Japan, competing against seven other teams.
stories.bodyText:
Top-order batter Pratika Rawal has been included in India’s women’s cricket squad for the 2026 Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as a replacement for injured Jemimah Rodrigues.
Jemimah continues to recover from a hamstring injury she suffered while playing for Southern Brave in The Hundred on August 3. The injury had already ruled her out of the ongoing Women’s Asia Cup in Dubai and the Asian Games.
Rawal gets Asian Games call-up
Rawal was initially named as Jemimah’s replacement only for the Asia Cup, with no official word at the time on who would take her place in the Asian Games squad. However, a BCCI source confirmed on Wednesday that Rawal’s name was already included in the 15-member squad submitted for the Asian Games, meaning she will travel to Japan as Jemimah’s replacement.
The 17-year-old made her T20I debut during the ongoing Asia Cup and has been used at No. 3 by the Indian team management. She has scored 22, 10 and 4 in her three league-stage appearances so far.
A long road back for Rawal
Rawal’s return to international cricket came after a lengthy injury layoff. She had not played competitive T20 cricket since November 2024 before her Asia Cup call-up and was also forced to miss the 2026 Women’s Premier League after an ankle injury suffered during the 2025 Women’s ODI World Cup. 
She had been preparing to join Warwickshire for the One Day Cup in England when the India call came. UP Warriorz had bought her for Rs 50 lakh at the WPL auction last year, but she could not feature in the 2026 season.
India head to Japan as defending champions
India will enter the women’s cricket competition at the Asian Games as defending champions after beating Sri Lanka by 19 runs in the final of the previous edition in Hangzhou. The eight-team competition is scheduled to run from September 17 to 22, with India joined by Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Japan, Thailand, Malaysia and China.
India’s Asian Games squad:
 Harmanpreet Kaur (captain), Smriti Mandhana (vice-captain), Shafali Verma, Pratika Rawal, Bharti Fulmali, Richa Ghosh (WK), G Kamalini (WK), Deepti Sharma, Radha Yadav, Prema Rawat, Arundhati Reddy, Kranti Gaud, Renuka Singh, N Sree Charani and Nandni Sharma.

stories.headline: Another Asiad-bound wrestler tests positive
stories.bodyText:
India received another setback in the run-up to the Asian Games with a third wrestler, Deepak (Greco-Roman 67kg), testing positive for a banned substance.
As a result, India will lose his berth in the mega event.
According to sources, Deepak was tested during the Asian Games selection trials in Lucknow on May 31 and returned a positive result for Clomifene.
Earlier, Mukul Dahiya (freestyle 86kg) and Deepanshu (Greco-Roman 130kg) had tested positive for banned substances.
Consequently, India has lost three wrestling berths out of a total of 18.
Recently, the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI) had urged wrestlers to act responsibly on anti-doping matters. The WFI has been stressing that wrestlers staying out of the national camp without due permission is one of the causes behind the doping cases.

briefs.headline: Harshit Rana likely to miss Afghanistan T20Is; Asian Games in danger too
briefs.deck: Harshit Rana faced a setback when he sustained an injury during a recent match simulation, raising concerns about his participation in the upcoming T20Is against Afghanistan. Meanwhile, Washington Sundar and Nitish Kumar Reddy have received the green light to return to the team. Updates on Jasprit Bumrah’s status are anticipated shortly, paving the way for finalizing team preparations post these…
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Harshit Rana’s return to international cricket will take some more time as the speedster has injured himself during the match simulation, which was part of the Return to Play (RTP) protocol, on Tuesday. It is understood that the injury does not look good at the moment and has put a major question mark over his participation in both the Afghanistan T20Is and the upcoming Asian Games.
Harshit Rana sustained a hamstring injury in the third T20I against England at Trent Bridge earlier this year.
Rana injured his knee during India's warm-up match against South Africa in the lead-up to the 2026 Men's T20 World Cup and was subsequently ruled out of that tournament. He then underwent surgery and missed the Indian Premier League (IPL) 2026 as well while playing for Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR).
After completing his rehabilitation, Rana was added to the India squad for the third ODI against Afghanistan in Chennai on June 20.
As TOI.com reported earlier, Nitish Kumar Reddy has received the all-clear, and Washington Sundar too has ticked the right boxes. With regard to Jasprit Bumrah, clarity is expected before the team links up to commence its preparations.
India will play Afghanistan in three T20Is on September 13, 15 and 17. Although the matches are being played in Delhi, Afghanistan are the official hosts of the bilateral series.
The Indian team will depart for the Asian Games from Delhi on September 18. Before the start of the Asian Games, Team India will also play a solitary T20I against Japan on September 22 at the Sano International Cricket Ground in Tochigi Prefecture.

briefs.headline: Big boost for India ahead of Afghanistan T20Is as Nitish Kumar Reddy clears fitness test
briefs.deck: Nitish Kumar Reddy has cleared his fitness test and is set to join the India squad ahead of the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan. The all-rounder, who missed recent white-ball tours due to a quadriceps injury, has also been named in India's squad for the upcoming Asian Games.
briefs.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: All-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy has received the green signal from the BCCI medical staff and is set to join the rest of the India squad in the national capital on Thursday ahead of the three-match T20I series against Afghanistan, starting on September 13, the TimesofIndia.com can confirm.
Reddy last played for India in the ODI series against Afghanistan earlier this year in June, where he aggravated his left quadriceps injury. The 23-year-old had initially sustained the injury while bowling in the first ODI in Dharamsala and was subsequently rested for the second match in Lucknow. Reddy returned for the third ODI in Chennai, where he experienced discomfort again. He then missed India's recent white-ball tours of Ireland and England because of the injury.
It is learnt that Reddy passed his fitness test last week, following which he was picked for the Afghanistan series. On Wednesday, he underwent a final match simulation at the 
BCCI
's Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru, which he passed in flying colours. It also is understood that he is bowling workload ticked all boxes and he seems ready for even the longer grind.
Reddy is also part of India's squad for the Asian Games, which begin on September 24. 
India won the men's gold medal at the previous edition of the Asian Games in Hangzhou, China, in October 2023. They were adjudged winners on the basis of being the higher-seeded team in the final against Afghanistan after the match was washed out.
Indian team will depart for Asian Games from Delhi on September 18. Before the start of the Asian Games, Team India will also play a solitary T20I against Japan n September 22 at the Sano International Cricket Ground in Tochigi Prefecture
